effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative outputs are AHP priority weights, consistency ratios (CR), and consensus rates rather than statistical treatment effects or regression coefficients; slight rounding differences appear between text (13.7%, 12.5%, 11.4%) and Table 2 (14%, 13%, 11%).
effect_estimate.value: AHP multi-criteria prioritization (N = 8 RWS entities; no regression or causal effect estimate reported): Social criteria ranked highest for RWS sustainability (45%), followed by economic (36%) and environmental (19%) criteria (CR = 0.001702, consensus = 85.8%; Table 1), with community-based management (25%), financial management (14%), community participation (12%), and willingness to pay (11%) ranked as top sub-criteria. Among four post-construction financing options, Community Financing via user tariffs ranked highest at 62%, followed by Private Financing (13.7% in text; 14% in Table 2), Grant Funding (12.5% in text; 13% in Table 2), and Debt Financing (11.4% in text; 11% in Table 2) (CR = 0.00482, consensus = 81%; Table 2). Stakeholder interviews found that lack of formal legal status and weak financial governance prevent most RWS from accessing formal credit (requiring personal guarantees when borrowing from banks or cooperatives), while tariffs set by community consensus fall below full cost recovery, leaving several RWS unable to fund pump and pipeline repairs and causing them to cease operations.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 3-4, Section 3 Result and Discussion, Table 1, and Table 2

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at <=2 by the non-experimental mixed-methods design. Assigned 2 because primary stakeholder interviews with RWS operators, the Association of Bantul RWS, and the Village and Community Empowerment Office directly document how lack of formal legal status bars RWS from formal credit (forcing reliance on personal guarantees) and how community-consensus tariffs below full cost recovery cause inability to repair pumps/pipelines and cessation of operations, though qualitative reporting is concise.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 3-4, Section 3 Result and Discussion

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines connection fees and monthly user tariffs set via community consensus below full cost recovery (BURDEN / fees), lack of formal legal status/recognition preventing RWS eligibility for formal bank credit (ELIGIBILITY), community-based management and community participation in RWS governance and tariff setting (participation), and fragmented resource management among providers (institutional_fragmentation).
